title: The periodic table: classification of elements
summary: The periodic table arranges elements by atomic number into periods, groups and blocks. Explain periodic trends, the chemistry of groups 1 and 17 and oxides, and use oxidation states; at HL, transition elements and their coloured complexes.

keyterms.definition: A horizontal row of the periodic table; the period number equals the number of occupied main energy levels.
A vertical column; elements in a group have the same number of valence electrons and similar chemistry.
Region of the table named after the sublevel being filled by the highest-energy electron.
Half the distance between nuclei of two bonded atoms of the same element; decreases across a period, increases down a group.
Energy change when one mole of electrons is added to one mole of gaseous atoms to form one mole of gaseous 1− ions.
Reduction in the attraction of the nucleus for outer electrons caused by repulsion from inner electrons.
Net positive charge felt by outer electrons; increases across a period because shielding stays similar while protons increase.
The charge an atom would have if all its bonds were ionic; written with sign first, e.g. +2, or as a Roman numeral in names.
An oxide that reacts with both acids and bases, e.g. Al₂O₃.
An element with properties intermediate between metals and non-metals, e.g. Si, Ge.
An element whose atoms have, or form ions with, an incomplete d sublevel.
A molecule or anion with a lone pair that forms a coordination bond to a central metal ion in a complex.
A central metal ion bonded to ligands by coordination bonds, e.g. [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺.
In a complex, ligands split the d orbitals into two energy levels; electron transitions between them absorb visible light.
Attraction to a magnetic field by species with unpaired electrons; diamagnetic species have all electrons paired.

questions.prompt: An element is in period 3 and group 15. Which is it?
questions.explanation: Period 3 has three occupied shells; group 15 has five valence electrons: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p³ is phosphorus.

questions.statement: Atomic radius decreases across a period.
questions.explanation: Nuclear charge increases while shielding is roughly constant, pulling the outer electrons closer.

questions.prompt: Why is a Na⁺ ion smaller than a Na atom?
options: It has lost its outer shell
questions.explanation: Na⁺ (2,8) has one fewer occupied shell than Na (2,8,1).
Bonding electrons are further from the nucleus and more shielded, so they are attracted less.

questions.prompt: Match each element to its block.
questions.explanation: The block is the sublevel the highest-energy electron occupies.
These are isoelectronic (18 e⁻); Cl⁻ has the fewest protons, so the weakest pull on the electrons.

questions.statement: First ionization energy increases down group 1.
questions.explanation: The outer electron is further away and more shielded, so it is easier to remove: IE decreases down a group.

questions.prompt: Order the period 3 elements by increasing atomic radius.
questions.explanation: Radius falls across the period, so the smallest is chlorine.

questions.text: Silicon, with properties between a metal and non-metal, is called a ___.
questions.explanation: Metalloids such as Si and Ge are semiconductors.

questions.prompt: Which element has the highest electronegativity?
questions.explanation: Fluorine (4.0) is the most electronegative element: small atom, high effective nuclear charge.

lessons.title: Group chemistry, oxides and oxidation states

questions.prompt: Which is the product when sodium reacts with water?
questions.explanation: 2Na(s) + 2H₂O(l) → 2NaOH(aq) + H₂(g).

questions.statement: Reactivity of group 1 metals increases down the group.
questions.explanation: The outer electron is lost more easily as atoms get larger.
A more reactive halogen (higher in the group) displaces a less reactive one from its halide.

questions.text: Sulfur trioxide dissolves in water to form an ___ solution.
questions.explanation: SO₃ + H₂O → H₂SO₄. Non-metal oxides are generally acidic.

questions.prompt: Match each oxide to its character.
questions.explanation: Oxides change from basic to amphoteric to acidic across period 3.

questions.prompt: What is the oxidation state of Mn in KMnO₄?
questions.explanation: K is +1, each O is −2: +1 + x − 8 = 0 → x = +7.

questions.text: The oxidation state of S in H₂SO₄ is ___.

questions.statement: The oxidation state of oxygen in H₂O₂ is −2.
questions.explanation: In peroxides each O is −1: 2(+1) + 2x = 0 → x = −1.

questions.prompt: Rain dissolving NO₂ and SO₂ from the air causes…
questions.explanation: Non-metal oxides form acids (HNO₃, H₂SO₄) that lower rain pH.

questions.prompt: Order the halogens by reactivity, most reactive first.
questions.explanation: Down group 17 atoms get bigger, so they gain an electron less readily.

questions.prompt: Why is zinc not considered a transition element?
options: Its only ion, Zn²⁺, has a full 3d¹⁰ sublevel
questions.explanation: Transition elements have (or form ions with) an incomplete d sublevel; Zn and Zn²⁺ both have 3d¹⁰.

questions.statement: Transition elements show variable oxidation states because 4s and 3d electrons are close in energy.
questions.explanation: Different numbers of electrons can be lost for similar energy cost, e.g. Fe²⁺ and Fe³⁺.

questions.prompt: What is the oxidation state of Cr in [Cr(H₂O)₄Cl₂]⁺?
questions.explanation: Water is neutral; two Cl⁻ give −2: x − 2 = +1 → x = +3.

questions.text: A ligand must have at least one ___ pair to donate to the metal ion.
questions.explanation: Ligands are Lewis bases that form coordination bonds.

options: It has a full d sublevel
It absorbs light in the orange/red region as d electrons move between split d levels
questions.explanation: The complementary colour of the absorbed light (orange/red) is seen: blue.
Sc³⁺ has no d electrons (3d⁰), so no d–d transitions can occur.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its example.
questions.explanation: Coordination number = number of coordination bonds to the metal.
Zn²⁺ (3d¹⁰) has all electrons paired; the others have unpaired d electrons.

questions.text: The coordination number of the metal in [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ is ___.
questions.explanation: Six ammonia ligands each form one coordination bond.

questions.prompt: Order the steps in explaining why a complex is coloured.
items: d orbitals split into two energy levels
Visible light of energy ΔE is absorbed
An electron is promoted to a higher d orbital
The complementary colour is transmitted and seen
questions.explanation: Colour depends on the size of the splitting ΔE, which depends on the metal, its oxidation state and the ligand.
